evidence.note: Colorado has roughly 32 active PM2.5 monitors statewide. Beyond maxTrustedDistanceMiles a reading describes a different airshed, so the engine reports advisory confidence instead of a firm call. On 2021-08-07 Longmont read 121.0 while Boulder CU read 74.6 in the same hour, 14 miles apart — which is why spread is a gate.

rules.rationale: Particulate is in the Good band. No activity restriction indicated.

precautions: Name a staff member watching for symptoms
rules.rationale: Hard exercise raises ventilation roughly sixfold, so a Moderate concentration delivers a much larger dose to an athlete with asthma than to a bystander.

precautions: Allow athletes to self-remove without penalty
rules.rationale: Moderate band with sustained moderate exertion is tolerable for most sensitive athletes with precautions in place.
Moderate band. No restriction indicated for athletes without a respiratory condition.
This band is defined by harm to sensitive groups. Sensitive athletes should not train outdoors in it at any intensity.
Vigorous effort multiplies inhaled dose enough to push an Unhealthy-for-Sensitive-Groups concentration into a harmful exposure for healthy athletes.
Dose scales with duration, so shortening the session is the proportionate response at this concentration.
Low-ventilation activity at this concentration delivers a modest dose.

precautions: Offer an indoor alternative if ventilation is filtered
rules.rationale: Sustained exercise in the Unhealthy band is not made safe by modification. Cancel or move the session.
Even low-exertion outdoor time is not advised in the Unhealthy band.
At these concentrations outdoor activity is contraindicated for everyone.
